newsitem.title: USA: Third L.A. student athlete dies in freak accident.
newsitem.headline: Third L.A. student athlete dies in freak accident.

text.p: The third Los Angeles area high school athlete to die in a freak accident in two weeks was taken off a life-support system on Monday after his organs had been removed to be donated, officials said.

Kriston Palomo, 16, was fatally injured during a school baseball game on Saturday when his larynx was crushed by the bill of a base runner's batting helmet as the two collided while Palomo was trying to catch a ball hit high in the air.

A spokesman for St. Bernard's Roman Catholic School said Palomo was the star of the school's baseball team and the team might not continue the rest of its season because of the tragedy. A decision was to be made later on Monday following a memorial service.

Surgery to remove Palomo's liver, corneas, and heart valves was carried out Sunday and he was removed from the life-support system early Monday morning. His parents had requested that he be kept on the system so his organs could be removed for donation, a hospital spokeswoman said.
On April 29, Heath Taylor, 17, a member of the William S. Hart High School track and field team, died after a pole vaulting accident when he bounced off the landing pad and hit the ground head first.
On April 22, Craig Kelford, 16, of Peninsula High School, died after being struck in the back of the head by a discus thrown by another athlete.
